These support documented risk and official actions but do not prove Putin personally ordered each facility-risk event.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: restricted domestic media and civil society could conceal safeguards failures, internal dissent, or misconduct.","duplicate_reporting":"E006-E010 and E021-E023 overlap on nuclear signaling and facility risk; they are not all independent underlying facts. E002/E003 are one HRW family. E049 adds distinct safeguards evidence.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both adverse and mitigating searches are represented through facility-risk evidence, E022's arms-control context, E023's treaty-compliant notification, and E049's safeguards material. Internal safeguards and governance checks remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Internal Russian safeguards or chain-of-command records, independent Russian-language technical reporting, and facility-level implementation audits are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E001 establishes formal authority. E022, E023, and E049 independently check selected signaling, treaty, and safeguards issues, but internal control implementation remains unverified.","open_system_complaint_volume":"International monitoring may overrepresent visible external nuclear incidents, but this is secondary to concealed-risk concerns and does not negate documented facility exposure.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Formal authority, facility exposure, arms-control baseline, and wartime shocks are addressed. Internal governance, broader population exposure, and target-period personal attribution remain incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E001","E005","E006","E007","E008","E009","E010","E021","E022","E023","E034","E049"],"unresolved_risks":["Personal attribution remains partly inferential.","Internal safeguards and expert deliberations are not documented.","Closed-system silence limits negative inference."]},"chapter_id":"1B","defensible_evidence_estimate":10,"independent_source_family_estimate":8,"missing_themes":["Internal safeguards and expert governance","Chain-of-command or personal-attribution evidence","Independent technical assessment of dual-use and facility-risk management"],"substantive_issues":["Material attribution and governance gaps remain research-recoverable.","Facility-risk evidence must not be presented as proof of a personal order by Putin."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E005 is an ICJ order; E011 contains Commission findings; E012 concerns an ICC warrant based on reasonable grounds; E034 is an indictment; E050 is disputed reporting. E040-E041 document cooperation and diplomatic alternatives, not proof of good faith or durable restraint.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: restricted reporting and conflict-access limitations may conceal military misconduct, internal dissent, or failed remedies.","duplicate_reporting":"The cited institutions are distinct, but E005, E011, E012, E016, E039-E041, and E047 may overlap on underlying events. E002/E003 are one HRW family. Claim-level deduplication remains necessary.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both adverse and contrary evidence are documented, including negotiated cooperation and diplomatic alternatives in E040-E041 and disputed settlement reporting in E050. Internal deliberations, tested counterclaims, proxy control, and remedy implementation remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Internal decision records, proxy-control evidence, local-language conflict reporting, and independent verification of remedy implementation are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E001 and E047 support formal authority and a decision chain; E005, E011, E012, and E039 provide external checks. Proxy control, internal deliberation, and remedy attribution remain unresolved.","open_system_complaint_volume":"International conflict-monitoring systems can concentrate reports where access and scrutiny are greatest; complaint volume is not a prevalence estimate, though documented findings remain material.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Conflict exposure, formal authority, legal findings, diplomatic alternatives, negotiated cooperation, and external shocks are addressed. Proxy control, inherited military baseline, remedy, and counterfactual alternatives remain incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E001","E005","E011","E012","E016","E039","E040","E041","E047","E050"],"unresolved_risks":["Attribution for subordinate or proxy conduct remains incomplete.","Remedy evidence shows gaps but not responsibility for denial.","Internal deliberations and official counterclaims are insufficiently tested.","E050 remains disputed and should not be treated as conclusive."]},"chapter_id":"2B","defensible_evidence_estimate":11,"independent_source_family_estimate":9,"missing_themes":["Internal deliberations and decision alternatives","Proxy or subordinate control","Implementation of remedy and corrective action","Independent testing of official counterclaims"],"substantive_issues":["Major events and contrary material are documented, but attribution and remedy remain research-recoverable gaps.","Negotiated cooperation must remain bounded contrary evidence, not general exculpation."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E024-E027 and E051-E052 document reported repression, prison conditions, and political-prisoner estimates, but are not uniformly adjudicated findings. Formal authority does not establish Putin's personal direction of every violation.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: criminalized dissent, surveillance, self-censorship, and civil-society exit suppress abuse reporting and national prevalence measurement.","duplicate_reporting":"E002/E003 are one HRW family. E024 and E025 may overlap on protest events despite independent organizations. E051/E052 come from one State Department report and should not be treated as separate source families.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse evidence is broad and includes vulnerable groups, prisons, detention, and remedy pressure. A targeted search for lawful restraint, effective remedies, and independently tested official justifications remains incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent inside-Russia or local-language monitoring, prison-remedy records, and denominator-based national prevalence data are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E001 supports formal authority, but official justifications, restraint claims, and remedy performance have not been independently tested.","open_system_complaint_volume":"High risk for apparent severity and prevalence: accessible international and civil-society reporting may overrepresent observable complaints. OVD-Info explicitly warns that reporting volume reflects observer access.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Protesters, journalists, monitors, LGBT+ people, prisoners, and political detainees are represented, with invasion and mobilization as shocks. National prevalence, prison-population denominators, and baseline change remain incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E001","E002","E003","E004","E024","E025","E026","E027","E051","E052"],"unresolved_risks":["Closed-system silence and open-system visibility bias coexist.","National prevalence and prison-remedy evidence remain incomplete.","Formal authority does not establish personal direction of every government-actor violation."]},"chapter_id":"3B","defensible_evidence_estimate":11,"independent_source_family_estimate":6,"missing_themes":["Prison-wide remedies and conditions beyond reported cases","National prevalence denominators","Direct incitement or authorization nexus","Balanced search for restraint and corrective action"],"substantive_issues":["Continuation can materially improve prevalence, detention, and attribution coverage.","Complaint counts must not be treated as national prevalence."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E028-E029 provide domestic election-monitoring observations with explicit reporting limitations; E002-E003 document restrictions and repression. E019 and E058 are inherited institutional context, not 2022 findings. E046 establishes a transparency restriction, not personal wrongdoing.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: media closures, surveillance, criminalized dissent, and self-censorship can conceal electoral and accountability failures.","duplicate_reporting":"E002/E003 are one HRW family. E028/E029 use overlapping Golos observation networks and should not be treated as fully independent event sets. E019 and E058 are distinct inherited-context sources.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse 2022 contestability evidence and inherited technically competent administration are both present. A complete target-period search for institutional checks, appointments, succession, official claims, and effective remedies is not documented.","missing_source_type":"2022 appointment and succession records, independent institutional-accountability outcomes, local-language investigative reporting, and independently verified official claims are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E001 establishes formal authority but not accountability. E028-E029 provide independent domestic monitoring; broader institutional checks and official claims remain incompletely tested.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Golos explicitly warns that report volume reflects observer activity and cannot measure total misconduct. External scrutiny may still concentrate visible complaints in a restricted information environment.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"E019 supplies inherited baseline; E028-E029 supply 2022 election evidence; E002-E003 supply restrictions; E055 supplies patronage context. The separation of inherited constraints, 2022 change, appointments, and succession remains incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E001","E002","E003","E019","E024","E025","E027","E028","E029","E046","E055","E058"],"unresolved_risks":["Appointments and succession remain uncovered.","Inherited baseline versus 2022 deterioration is only partly separated.","Closed-system silence limits negative inference.","Institutional remedy outcomes are missing."]},"chapter_id":"4B","defensible_evidence_estimate":11,"independent_source_family_estimate":7,"missing_themes":["2022 appointments and succession","Institutional accountability and remedy outcomes","Complete official and contrary evidence audit"],"substantive_issues":["Target-period election evidence materially improves the chapter but does not resolve succession or institutional-accountability gaps.","E019 and E058 must remain inherited context only."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E013/E017 are official instructions, not implementation findings. E014/E015/E035 provide macroeconomic context; E032-E034 concern networks, sanctions, or procurement and do not establish Putin's personal enrichment or responsibility for aggregate outcomes.","closed_system_silence":"Medium-to-high risk: restricted media and civic space can suppress reporting of household hardship, capture, procurement abuse, and implementation failure.","duplicate_reporting":"E013/E017 are one source family. E014/E015/E035 overlap in macroeconomic shock and contraction analysis. E032/E033 are one Treasury family. E030-E031 and E044 overlap as OCCRP/LLCInvest network research.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both policy-response and adverse-shock evidence are present, including Central Bank stabilization. Distributional harms, implementation failures, capture, enrichment, and correction were not systematically searched.","missing_source_type":"Household and regional distribution data, independent implementation audits, procurement and ownership findings, and local-language reporting are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E013/E017 establish policy intent. E014/E015/E035 independently assess macro conditions; E036/E048 provide institutional response evidence. None independently verifies presidential authorship, household delivery, or personal benefit.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Not the principal risk because the main evidence is macroeconomic rather than complaint-count based. Visible household complaints could still overrepresent accessible or politically salient hardship.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Formal direction, sanctions and war shocks, macro outcomes, and Central Bank response are addressed. Household distribution, regional exposure, inherited baseline, implementation, and correction remain unclear.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E013","E014","E015","E032","E034","E035","E036","E048"],"unresolved_risks":["Aggregate outcomes cannot stand in for household welfare or ruler effectiveness.","War and sanctions confound attribution.","Capture, enrichment, delivery, and correction evidence remain incomplete.","E045 is discovery-only and excluded."]},"chapter_id":"5B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":6,"missing_themes":["Household and regional distribution","Independent implementation and delivery audit","Directly attributed capture or enrichment findings","Correction and adaptive response"],"substantive_issues":["The chapter has improved source breadth but still lacks delivery and distribution evidence.","GDP contraction and financial stabilization should not be converted into ruler credit or blame without attribution and exposure evidence."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E013/E017 establish stated support instructions, not delivery. E037-E038 and E043-E054 provide country or institutional outcomes and actions, not personal responsibility. No adjudicated adverse or favorable ruler-specific finding is presented.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: restricted monitoring can conceal unequal access, service failures, politicization, and mortality-reporting problems.","duplicate_reporting":"E013/E017 are one Kremlin family. E037/E042/E043/E054 are WHO-family materials; E042 is a weak lead. E014/E015 are economic context, not independent health-delivery evidence. E053 is distinct survey evidence.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Favorable intent and limited institutional action are present through E013, E036, and E043. Searches for delivery failure, equity, affordability, mortality validation, durable outcomes, and corrective response remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent health-system delivery audits, regional and household equity data, mortality and immunization validation, affordability evidence, and local-language or NGO monitoring are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E013 is official intent; E037/E038, E043, and E053 provide independent outcome, data-quality, and access context. They do not independently verify delivery reach or presidential contribution.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Secondary risk: international reporting may overrepresent accessible or salient failures, but underreporting and unreliable denominators in a restricted system are more consequential.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Beneficiaries, health-system structure, unmet needs, macro shocks, data limitations, and one target-period pilot are addressed. Actual reach, subgroup and regional equity, inherited baseline, affordability, durability, and correction remain unresolved.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E013","E014","E015","E036","E037","E038","E043","E053","E054"],"unresolved_risks":["Direct independent evidence of delivery and equity remains limited.","Country-level outcomes cannot establish ruler-attributed performance.","Closed-system silence and mortality-data limitations materially reduce confidence.","Missing evidence is not evidence of poor performance."]},"chapter_id":"6B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Delivery quality and population reach","Equity and affordability","Independent mortality and immunization validation","Politicization, correction, and durability"],"substantive_issues":["The continuation improved domain coverage but not ruler attribution or delivery verification.","Further bounded research could materially improve regional reach, affordability, and independent outcome validation."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E030/E031/E044 are investigative and network-level allegations; E032/E033/E055/E059 are administrative sanctions findings, not criminal judgments; E046 establishes a transparency restriction, not enrichment; E060 cautions that sanctions work was incomplete. No final judicial enrichment adjudication is present.","closed_system_silence":"Very high risk: media restrictions, NGO exit, surveillance, and self-censorship can suppress corruption detection and publication.","duplicate_reporting":"E030, E031, and E044 overlap in LLCInvest/Putin-linked network research and are not three independent families. E032/E033 are one Treasury family. E055 is a distinct official sanctions family but overlaps conceptually with patronage claims. E018 is a context lead only.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse personal/network evidence is substantial, but largely investigative or administrative. Favorable evidence is limited to official declarations or denials; no systematic search for exculpatory records, independent audits, or lawful asset explanations is documented.","missing_source_type":"Court or enforcement findings, independently verified ownership and beneficial-ownership records, procurement evidence, appointment/conflict-of-interest records, and independent local-language investigative corroboration are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E032/E033/E055/E059 are official sanctions assessments with stated bases but no independent judicial check. E046 is an official transparency notice. Credible independent exculpatory verification is absent.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Open investigations may overrepresent opposition-linked or visible allegations and make severity appear higher. This is secondary to severe closed-system underreporting and does not convert allegations into findings.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Network exposure, alleged personal nexus, official opacity, appointment/patronage context, and target-period records are addressed. Verified personal ownership or benefit, inherited wealth separation, and 2022-specific conduct remain incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E018","E030","E031","E032","E033","E044","E046","E047","E055","E059","E060"],"unresolved_risks":["The personal nexus is credible but remains partly contested and non-adjudicated.","Opacity is not proof of concealment motive.","A bounded search for court findings, financial records, and independent corroboration could materially improve the dossier.","E060 limits interpretation of sanctions as final adjudication."]},"chapter_id":"7B","defensible_evidence_estimate":7,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Adjudicated personal-integrity findings","Verified ownership and beneficial-ownership records","Appointment or conflict-of-interest nexus","Independent favorable or exculpatory evidence"],"substantive_issues":["The chapter now contains credible personal/network evidence, but it remains allegation- and designation-heavy.","Continuation is warranted for adjudication, ownership verification, and balanced exculpatory searching."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E013/E017 are official instructions; E034 is an indictment; E036/E048 are institutional reports; E035 is macro context; E056 is official domestic monitoring; E057 is independent analysis. These establish intent, assigned responsibility, or institutional action, not comprehensive successful implementation or durable progress.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: restricted reporting can conceal bureaucratic distortion, implementation failure, dissenting performance information, and lack of correction.","duplicate_reporting":"E013/E017 are one source family. E035/E036 overlap in crisis-response context despite distinct institutions. E037/E042/E043/E054 are WHO-family materials. E056/E057 overlap on mobilization failures but are distinct source families. Some operational outcomes remain institutionally rather than ruler attributed.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both favorable and adverse material are present: E036, E040, E043, E048, and E060 document institutional action, cooperation, or adaptation, while E025, E034, E035, E056, and E057 document coercive execution, procurement allegations, adverse outcomes, or implementation failures. Independent audits, competence comparisons, correction, and durable results remain incompletely searched.","missing_source_type":"Independent implementation audits, bureaucratic competence measures, subnational delivery data, procurement oversight, and local-language performance reporting are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E013/E017 establish official intent; E036/E048 and E056 provide institution-specific implementation evidence; E034, E035, and E057 provide narrower external checks. No comprehensive independent audit of the governing portfolio is present.","open_system_complaint_volume":"International analysis may overrepresent visible or politically salient failures. Restricted scrutiny may more importantly hide performance failures and suppress complaint reporting.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Formal authority, assigned bodies, war and sanctions shocks, selected implementation actions, mobilization failures, and limited cooperation are addressed. Population-level delivery, inherited administrative baseline, subnational variation, competence, and durability remain unclear.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E001","E013","E014","E015","E016","E025","E034","E035","E036","E040","E041","E043","E048","E056","E057","E060"],"unresolved_risks":["Official intent remains stronger than independently verified effectiveness.","External shocks confound outcome attribution.","The evidence does not cover the complete program portfolio or durable progress.","Subnational and population exposure remain weakly measured."]},"chapter_id":"8B","defensible_evidence_estimate":15,"independent_source_family_estimate":9,"missing_themes":["Independent implementation audits","Personnel competence and bureaucratic execution","Subnational and population-level delivery","Correction after failure","Durable goal progress"],"substantive_issues":["The high unit count does not resolve execution, competence, or durability gaps.","Institutional action should not be converted into direct presidential credit without an authority and outcome nexus."]}],"global_findings":["No researcher-written scores, ranges, anchors, rankings, or judge instructions are present.","All eight selected chapters retain at least one material, bounded, research-recoverable attribution, contrary-evidence, source-quality, event-coverage, or implementation gap.","Closed-system silence is the principal cross-chapter bias; absence of domestic reporting is not exculpatory.","Open-system complaint volume and duplicated reporting require cautious interpretation; complaint counts are not prevalence estimates.","E013/E017, E002/E003, E030/E031/E044, E032/E033, Golos materials, and WHO materials require family-aware counting. Discovery-only E045 and weak lead E042 are excluded from defensible estimates.","Local facts are appropriately treated as contextual priors with attribution warnings; unused local facts are not evidence defects.","The remaining continuation should stay bounded to the selected chapter lenses and target attribution, contrary evidence, precise locators, remedy, delivery, adjudication, and target-period separation."],"needs_continuation":true,"reviewer_summary":"Continuation remains warranted for all eight selected chapters. The latest round materially improved coverage, including safeguards, prisons, health access, mobilization failures, and personal/network evidence, but did not resolve the principal research-recoverable gaps: closed-system silence, incomplete ruler attribution, weak independent delivery or remedy auditing, incomplete contrary or exculpatory searches, and limited adjudicated evidence in 7B. Missing evidence is not treated as negative ruler evidence.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":["1B","2B","3B","4B","5B","6B","7B","8B"]}
